Log-concave spline smoothing of a discrete convolution kernel estimate

Source: R/log_conc_smooth.R
log_conc_smooth.Rd

Fits a concave quadratic B-spline (via cobs) to \(\log_{10}(y + \varepsilon)\) and back-transforms and normalises the fit so the result is a **log-concave, non-negative, unit L1 norm** smoothed version of the original convolution kernel estimate \(y\). A small offset is added internally to avoid taking the logarithm of zero; the final vector is renormalised to unit L1 norm.

Usage

log_conc_smooth(y, tau = 0.5, nknots = NULL)

Arguments

y

numeric vector (length \(n \ge 3\)) with the raw, non-negative data sampled at the integer points 1:length(y).

tau

quantile to be fitted by cobs; defaults to 0.5 (median fit).

nknots

integer; number of interior knots for the spline. If NULL (default) it is set to round(length(y)/5).

Value

A numeric vector of length length(y):

  • strictly non-negative,

  • log-concave over its support,

  • rescaled to unit L1 norm.

Details

The weights passed to cobs() are proportional to y + offs, where offs = max(y) * 1e-6; in practice that gives the most stable fits for sparse or strongly peaked inputs.

See also

cobs for the underlying constrained B-spline regression.

Author

Tom Wenseleers tom.wenseleers@kuleuven.be \ Laboratory of Socioecology and Social Evolution, KU Leuven \ https://bio.kuleuven.be/eeb/tw/research \ ORCID: 0000-0002-1434-861X

Examples

if (requireNamespace("cobs", quietly = TRUE)) {
set.seed(1)
x      <- seq(-5, 5, length.out = 101)

## underlying "true" density on the grid
f_true <- dnorm(x)
f_true <- f_true / sum(f_true)          # ensure it integrates to 1

N      <- 100000                        # total expected counts
lambda <- N * f_true                    # Poisson means in each bin

y_cnt  <- rpois(length(x), lambda)      # Poisson-noisy counts
y      <- y_cnt / sum(y_cnt)            # rescale back to a density

g <- log_conc_smooth(y)

matplot(cbind(y, f_true, g), type = "l", lty = 1,
        col = c(2, 1, 4), ylab = "density",
        main = "Raw (Poisson) vs. log-concave smoothed curve + ground truth")
legend("topleft", legend = c("raw (Poisson)", "smoothed", "ground truth"),
       col = c(2, 4, 1), lty = 1, bty = "n")
}
